name: Improperly Controlled Sequential Memory Allocation
principle: The product does not correctly control the sequence and completion of operations that allocate or dispatch bounded work, such as queue, callback, or control-flow steps.
detection_signals: Queue or callback work is enqueued, dispatched, or reclaimed in an order that violates the producer or consumer contract
Sequential allocation or retry work has no enforced completion, reclamation, or ordering condition
A callback or queue entry can be consumed before initialization or can remain active after its owner is released
negative_signals: The producer, consumer, and cleanup order is explicit and checked at each transition
Queue entries have bounded ownership and are reclaimed exactly once after completion
Callbacks cannot run before initialization or after the owning resource is released
false_defense_traps: Treating a queue API name as proof that enqueue and dequeue order is safe
Adding a retry or allocation limit without fixing callback ownership or completion order
Classifying the mechanism as resource exhaustion merely because allocation occurs
verification_focus: Are initialization, enqueue/dispatch, completion, and reclamation steps ordered and bounded according to their actual producer-consumer contract?
patch_principle: Define and enforce the lifecycle order for each queued or callback operation
Reject or defer consumption until initialization is complete
Reclaim completed work exactly once and before owner teardown
